evidence.detail: Apr 18 2024 'Show cards in order of interestingness in rotation hype message' — added list_of_most_interesting() with sorting by cardfeed rank; never-before-legal cards receive rank 1 (highest priority)

list_of_most_interesting() sorts by (rank or 999999, name); never-before-legal cards get rank 1 via oracle query so they sort first; Footbottom Feast (legal before, played) now appears after never-before-legal and heavily-played cards

triage.notes: The fixing commit cited #9165 (a separate issue) but the behavior change directly addresses the ordering complaint in #12244. Issue can be closed.
triage.proposed_comment: The ordering fix was shipped in commit 20a87a97 (April 2024): hype message cards are now sorted by interestingness — never-before-legal cards rank first, then by cardfeed play-rate rank, so a previously-legal lightly-played card like Footbottom Feast will appear well down the list.

own_evidence.detail: Commit message says 'Fixes #9165', not #12244; was authored 4 days before issue #12244 was even opened, yet issue #12244 reports the problem persisting in the 84th run.

Never-before-legal cards get rank 1, previously-legal cards keep their cardfeed rank. If cardfeed rank 1 = most popular, popular previously-legal cards share rank 1 and intermix with never-before-legal cards, potentially allowing a lightly-played previously-legal card to still appear.
FetchException fallback skips the sort entirely, reverting to pre-fix behavior if cardfeed is unavailable.

Author bakert commented 'It's supposed to be ordering never-before-legal and heavily-played cards first' — phrasing suggests the fix did not fully work for this case, not that it was already resolved.

verify.refutation_reason: Issue #12244 was filed 4 days after commit 20a87a97, specifically reporting that the 84th run (which occurred after the fix) still showed Footbottom Feast. The commit itself references 'Fixes #9165', not this issue. The code's fallback behavior (no sort if cardfeed fails) and the ranking scheme (never-before-legal gets rank 1, same as most popular previously-legal cards) leave open the possibility of the problem recurring. Cannot independently confirm the fix resolves this specific report.
